items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first-ever trilateral
items.summary: the White House confirmed a meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday on the APEC sidelines, with nuclear arms reduction the headline topic and no agreement expected; Trump will raise Iran but not Ukraine.
items.matters: the three largest nuclear arsenals have had no caps since New START lapsed in February.
items.body: Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Chinese President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. AP; Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 13, 2026, 7:08 PM EST / Updated Nov. 13, 2026, 10:07 PM EST By Megan Shannon and Caroline Kenny President Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of China and Russia on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzen , China’s tech hub, next week, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world’s biggest nuclear powers. It is not anticipated that any sort of agreement will come from the trilateral meeting, according to a senior U.S. official, who described the session as an “entry point” and “the first conversation,” pointing to the reduction of nuclear arsenals as a key topic. “We do think it’s time for China to sort of step up, you know, to the adults’ table, if you will, and have adult conversations about adult things,” the senior U.S. official said about the issue of nuclear weapons. Beijing’s arsenal of more than 600 warheads , according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact. The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernized” deal that includes China. The three-way summit with Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin comes at a complicated moment in relations for the three countries. Trump has warmly embraced Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world’s foremost economic powers. Similarly, Trump has sought to build his relationship with Putin , even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly 5-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran. There is no bilateral with Putin scheduled, but the two leaders will appear at events and the trilateral meeting together, according to a senior U.S. official. There are no plans for Trump to engage with North Korea during the trip, according to a senior U.S. official. Separately, Elon Musk will be…

items.headline: FAA grounded every US departure for nearly five hours
items.summary: a telecommunications failure affecting air route traffic control centres halted departures nationwide before the order was lifted; more than 5,000 flights were cancelled and about 10,000 delayed.
items.matters: the third nationwide ground stop this century and the longest since 2001.

items.headline: Waloryzacja 2027: rząd przyjął rozporządzenie
items.summary: składnik płacowy zostaje na ustawowym minimum, czyli 20 proc. realnego wzrostu wynagrodzeń, a prognozowany wskaźnik to co najmniej 3,48 proc., z podwyżkami od 1 marca.
items.matters: przy tych prognozach najniższa emerytura pierwszy raz przekroczy 2 tys. zł brutto.
items.body: Jest już rozporządzenie dotyczące waloryzacji emerytur i rent w 2027 roku. Dokumentem został przyjęty przez Radę Ministrów i opublikowany w Dzienniku Ustaw. Wynika z niego, że wysokość zwiększenia wskaźnika waloryzacji pozostanie na ustawowym minimum, czyli 20 proc. realnego wzrostu przeciętnego wynagrodzenia. Decyzja zapadła po tym, jak Rada Dialogu Społecznego nie wypracowała wspólnego stanowiska. To jedna z pierwszych decyzji, które będą miały wpływ na wysokość przyszłorocznej waloryzacji emerytur i rent . Choć ostateczny wskaźnik podwyżki świadczeń będzie znany dopiero po opublikowaniu danych o inflacji i realnym wzroście wynagrodzeń za 2026 rok, rząd już teraz przesądził o jednym z jego kluczowych elementów. Rozporządzenie, które zostało już opublikowane w Dzienniku Ustaw, określa bowiem, że część waloryzacji związana z realnym wzrostem płac pozostanie na ustawowym minimum. To informacja istotna dla milionów emerytów i rencistów, ponieważ właśnie ten składnik – obok inflacji – współtworzy wskaźnik waloryzacji obowiązujący od 1 marca. Decyzja zapadła po fiasku negocjacji w Radzie Dialogu Społecznego, co uruchomiło ustawowy obowiązek wydania rozporządzenia przez Radę Ministrów. Rada Ministrów zaakceptowała i wydała rozporządzenie w sprawie wysokości zwiększenia wskaźnika waloryzacji emerytur i rent w 2027 roku . Dokument nie zmienia zasad waloryzacji określonych w ustawie, ale przesądza o jednym z najważniejszych elementów wpływających na wysokość przyszłorocznych podwyżek świadczeń. Jak wskazano w uzasadnieniu: „Świadczenia emerytalno-rentowe podlegają corocznie waloryzacji od dnia 1 marca.” To oznacza, że tradycyjnie podwyżki dla seniorów zostaną przeprowadzone z początkiem marca 2027 roku. Już na początku czerwca stanowisko rządu było jasne. Jak przypomniano w uzasadnieniu: „W dniu 9 czerwca 2026 r. Rada Ministrów przyjęła Propozycję zwiększenia wskaźnika waloryzacji emerytur i rent w 2027 r., w której strona rządowa proponuje Radzie Dialogu Społecznego pozostawienie zwiększenia wskaźnika waloryzacji emerytur i rent w 2027 r., na poziomie ustawowego minimum wynoszącego 20% realnego wzrostu przeciętnego wynagrodzenia w 2026 r.” Oznaczało to pozostawienie minimalnego poziomu przewidzianego w ustawie. Po braku porozumienia rząd musiał samodzielnie określić wysokość zwiększenia wskaźnika. Jak czytamy w uzasadnieniu: „W związku z nieuzgodnieniem, w ramach Rady Dialogu Społecznego, wysokości zwiększenia wskaźnika waloryzacji emerytur i rent w 2027 r. Rada Ministrów, biorąc pod uwagę informacje o prognozowanych wielkościach makroekonomicznych, w tym…

items.headline: Notion confirms AI chat transcripts were taken in the Fireworks breach
items.summary: fewer than 1% of workspaces were affected, most transcripts were unattributable, and Notion disabled its Insights feature and stopped serving open-weight models through Fireworks.
items.matters: the inference vendor, not the app, was the attack surface, and keys pasted into chats are now treated as exposed.
items.body: In addition to previously notifying the impacted customers, on November 12 we reported exposed third-party API keys found in affected user messages to the vendors that issued them. On November 11, we revoked exposed Notion API keys that were found in affected user messages during our investigation. This post informs you about the recent Fireworks AI Incident and how it’s impacting <1% of Notion workspaces. For the latest on the Fireworks AI incident, please see their official updates here . We have contacted our customers who were affected by the Fireworks incident. If you haven't heard from us, we haven't identified your workspace as affected, and no action is needed right now. Our investigation is ongoing. If we determine that your workspace was impacted, we will contact you directly. Upon analysis of the dataset Fireworks AI gave us on November 8, we discovered that it included Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, which for the vast majority of impacted workspaces were unattributable. "Unattributable" means the chats weren't labeled with who wrote them or which workspace they came from, and the transcripts did not contain tool call results. Beyond what’s in the chat transcript itself, there’s no information tying the chat back to workspaces, users, or companies. What is Fireworks AI and how we used them: Fireworks is one of the most used global AI infrastructure platforms powering tens of thousands of customers and used by hundreds of thousands of developers. We used Fireworks for classification jobs to help customers understand their own AI usage through a feature in Notion called Insights, and we used them as a general inference provider to serve open-weight models inside our product. The Insights feature has been disabled as we investigate this incident, and we are no longer serving open-weight models through Fireworks. What we recommend for affected customers: Affected customers are able to retrieve and review the impacted data securely inside their workspace, with instructions sent via email. We also recommend that affected customers treat this data as if it were exposed. If those with affected workspaces have pasted sensitive information, passwords, API keys, or other credentials into Notion AI during the timeframe of the incident, rotate them. We take your privacy and the security of your data seriously. Even though this was not a breach of our systems, keeping your data safe is fundamental to using Notion for your life’s work. It is our mission to make sure this never happens again. We will raise the standard for how your…

items.headline: SoftBank booked a $3.7bn charge on AI data-centre power gear
items.summary: the write-off on cancelled gas-turbine orders for US campuses drove a ¥1.12trn quarterly net loss, its first in almost two years.
items.matters: the first audited number showing how far electricity planning has run ahead of demand.
items.body: A cyberattack at Fireworks AI — a platform developers use to access open AI models — let hackers into a Fireworks development system through its cloud provider, exposing customer billing information and datasets. Notion confirmed this week that the hackers took chat transcripts of Notion AI customers who used the Insights feature. Notion said the breach affected around 1% of its customers and that much of the exposed chat data could not be attributed to a specific user or workspace; it disconnected from Fireworks on November 3. Fireworks says the hackers are financially motivated, selling stolen access to large language models — its second breach in as many…

items.headline: More than $3.2bn of Chinese AI data-centre projects are being re-planned
items.summary: Reuters reported builds around export-restricted H100, H200 and H800 chips facing delay, disruption or redesign as Washington tightens scrutiny after Huang's exit.
items.matters: the installed base of restricted silicon is now a policy problem, not only a compliance one.
items.body: Jensen Huang’s resignation collides with a new fight over AI-chip exports, nonprofits ask a California court to freeze frontier-model development, Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, and Whitehall turns back to in-person interviews after a surge in AI-generated applications. All 72 stories from the day, below. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid reports of a Chinese intelligence targeting effort and congressional scrutiny . In the fallout, congressional leaders described growing bipartisan support for tighter AI-chip export limits to China . A Reuters-based report says more than $3.2 billion in Chinese data-center projects built around restricted Nvidia chips now face delays, disruption, or redesign , while a nonprofit found at least 400 fake accounts amplifying defenses of Huang and support for Nvidia exports; at least 260 were deactivated or suspended on X . The leadership crisis is now entangled with export policy, infrastructure already built around restricted chips, and an online influence campaign. Four nonprofits asked a California court to freeze frontier-model development beyond current capabilities at five AI companies . Model and infrastructure expansion continued around that challenge: Google announced the speed-optimized Gemini 4 Hydrogen for Search and the Gemini app , a release tracker reported Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 , and Nscale said its active GPU fleet doubled to about 50,000 in two and a half months . The lawsuit targets further development just as model vendors and compute suppliers keep expanding. Employers are adjusting the human side of AI use. Whitehall plans more face-to-face interviews after AI-generated applications produced a growing number of unqualified candidates . In Bournemouth, JP Morgan’s 5,300-person campus and the surrounding finance sector face anxiety over automation of back-office and entry-level roles . Meanwhile, a Lenovo report found eight in ten IT decision-makers call the digital workplace critical to AI transformation, but only 10% have fundamentally redesigned it . And at a Hollywood panel, SAG-AFTRA and Vermillio laid out opposing approaches to digital replicas, consent, compensation, and unauthorized use . Across hiring, finance, workplace design, and performance, institutions are deciding where AI changes the work and where a person still has to be present, protected, or paid. items.headline: Blender 5.3 is out and 5.2 LTS moved to critical-fixes only
items.summary: 5.3.0 shipped on 9 November, 5.2.4 landed the same day, and 5.2's active support window ended on 10 November.
items.matters: anything in a Meddle or asset pipeline should either pin 5.2 LTS or move to 5.3 deliberately.
items.body: Since February 2023 , Blender follows a 3-releases-per-year schedule, with one of the releases offering long-term support (Blender LTS). Non-LTS releases are supported until the next release with high-priority bug fixes. High-severity and normal bugs may be fixed too if agreed on by the team. LTS releases are supported for 2 years. At first the support level is the same as non-LTS releases; but after the next release is out, they are supported with critical bugfixes only. You should be running one of the supported release numbers listed above in the rightmost column. blender --version Show Product Identifiers repology: blender cpe: cpe:/a:blender:blender cpe: cpe:2.3:a:blender:blender You can submit an improvement to this page on GitHub . Every game build we ingest, diffed field-by-field against the previous one: new and changed items, mounts, toys, spells, achievements and more. Read straight from the World of Warcraft client, not a rumour. Every entity in a build page links to its own page here, so a datamined mount or currency is one click from its full entry. World of Warcraft changes constantly. Blizzard releases patches that rebalance classes, add new content, and fix bugs. Between patches, they push hotfixes that address urgent problems. Beneath both lie datamined files extracted from the game client itself, showing what changes are coming before Blizzard officially announces them. If you play any version of WoW and want to stay competitive, make gold, or simply understand what's changing, you need to track this information. News matters differently depending on why you play. A player pushing mythic raids cares about class balance changes three weeks out. A gold maker watches for profession recipes before they go live and buys materials accordingly. Someone leveling a new character might care most about whether their rotation is getting buffed or nerfed this month. A transmog collector looks for new transmog sets and appearances added to the game. A healer might want to know if incoming damage patterns are changing, so they can plan cooldown rotations. A PvP player wants to know whether their spec is being balanced up or down. The beauty of datamined information is that it surfaces all of this at once, letting you pick what's relevant to you. TheWoWDB news section gives you every change ingested directly from the game client. It is not a rumor, not a leaked screenshot, and not an assumption. It is field-by-field data extracted from Blizzard's own files. Each build that Blizzard pushes to test or production servers is captured, compared to the previous build, and made available here. New items, changed item stats, removed quests, new achievements, modified spells, all of it is tracked. The difference between this and other sites is accuracy and comprehensiveness. Datamined data is automatically extracted, so nothing is missed and nothing is guessed at. If someone else reports a change but it is not in the game files, it will not appear here. items.headline: EU leaders held their first AI summit in Dublin
items.summary: Costa chaired with von der Leyen and Metsola in the room, Mistral's Arthur Mensch told them Europe has the technology but needs "speed, financing and strong coordination", and Geoffrey Hinton briefed on rights and jobs.
items.matters: no text was adopted, so the AI Act calendar is unchanged and the gigafactory money is still trapped in the 2028-2034 budget fight.
items.body: European Union leaders gather in Dublin on Friday for their first-ever summit devoted to artificial intelligence, debating how the bloc can catch up with the United States and China. The summit caps a week of marathon diplomacy in Ireland. On Thursday, Dublin’s Convention Centre hosted about 50 leaders from across the continent for the ninth summit of the European Political Community, themed around a strong, secure, and connected Europe, which Taoiseach Micheál Martin called “the biggest gathering of international leaders that Ireland has ever hosted”. European Council president António Costa called that meeting because, as he wrote in his invitation letter, “a first dedicated discussion, at leaders’ level, is now needed” on AI’s opportunities and its transformative effect on Europe’s economies. Two outside voices will brief the 27: Mistral chief executive Arthur Mensch, the standard-bearer for European AI sovereignty , and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, the field’s most prominent worrier. The agenda is competitiveness first: funding, red tape, and guardrails. The sharpest exhibit is the bloc’s own flagship. The plan to build seven AI gigafactories, data centres housing advanced processors, cloud, and connectivity under one roof, has yet to fully take off, snagged on the fight between member states over competitiveness spending in the 2028–2034 EU budget. The Commission’s InvestAI programme promised to mobilise €200B, including €20B for gigafactories; delays and funding stumbles have been piling up for months. The meeting lands after a year of incidents involving rogue AI agents, and a week in which Nvidia lost its CEO, leaving the industry without its laitmotive. Safety, once a Brussels speciality exported through safety pledges , is suddenly everyone’s agenda item. Also, Ukraine was added to the programme after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner flew into Dublin to meet President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who was already in town for the EPC, the envoys fresh from talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Per a senior EU official, leaders are likely to discuss Europe’s role in peace negotiations and the security guarantees the bloc could offer in a ceasefire. Europe called a meeting to plan its technological independence, and geopolitics walked in the door anyway. The Commission’s Apply AI Summit follows in Brussels on 17 November; what the leaders actually commit to today will show whether Dublin was a strategy session or a group photo. I am the Editor in Chief for TNW, covering technology not as a parade of launches and valuations, but as a system of…

items.body: EU leaders in Dublin were called on by an AI executive to move quickly in the tech race with the US and China. EU official Metsola, however, expressed frustration with the idea that the bloc is behind in AI development. The meeting took place in Dublin's Convention Center, which was also the meeting place of the European Political Community summit this week. French AI company Mistral's CEO Arthur Mensch, as well as Nobel-prize winner and researcher Geoffrey Hinton, widely known as the "godfather of AI," spoke to EU leaders at the summit. "Europe has all the technology and the talent to lead the AI race," Mensch said during the event. "What it needs is speed, financing and a strong coordination between member states." Mensch urged the leaders to "act now" to stay competitive with the US and China in regards to AI development. "AI is the most important technology of our time," European Council ‌President Antonio Costa said in a post on X regarding the summit. "Europe must make the most of its benefits, from higher productivity to better public services. We must also manage the risks and changes it will bring — and help set global standards for responsible governance and safe, human-centric AI." The summit took place at a time of mounting worries about the emerging technology, which promises to transform ‌industries, labor markets and societies. It also came in the wake of a series of incidents involving rogue AI agents in recent months and the wider discussion about how the technology could harm humanity. Tech leaders behind the technology have also fallen under scrutiny. As recently as this week, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was forced to resign after it was revealed that he had been in a relationship with a Chinese spy and a direct report in his company. During the summit, a discussion occurred about where Europe fits in within the AI movement. European Parliament President Roberta Metsola said she frustrated with the notion that Europe had "somehow lost the AI race." She noted that the EU has "world-class talent, technological expertise and industrial experience to lead in AI." "What we need now is to ensure that our ideas have the financing they need to grow and succeed in Europe," she added. Will AI laws protect us? items.body: The Personal Data Protection Board’s (Board) Principle Decision dated 1 July 2026 and numbered 2026/1301 was published in the Official Gazette dated 28 July 2026 and numbered 33323. The Board stated that personal data shared on the websites of institutions such as municipalities, universities, and special provincial administrations must be based on one of the conditions for processing personal data set out in the Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK) and must be relevant to, limited to, and proportionate to the purposes for which they are processed. Emphasizing the need to establish how long such data should remain publicly accessible, fulfill the obligation to inform, and implement appropriate security measures, the Board called for an urgent review of existing disclosures. On 28 July 2026, the Personal Data Protection Authority (Authority) also published a KVKK compliance guide for public institutions and professional organizations with public institution status. You may access the Authority’s announcement in Turkish here and the compliance guide in Turkish here . In its announcement dated 21 July 2026, the Authority emphasized that the use of personal data obtained from third parties for marketing purposes must be based on one of the conditions for processing personal data set out in Article 5 of the KVKK, such as explicit consent. It stated that the obligation to inform must be fulfilled within a reasonable period, or at the time of the first contact where the data is used for contact purposes, and separately from the explicit consent procedures, and that continuing a conversation or not communicating an objection does not, in itself, constitute explicit consent. Similarly, by its Decision dated 10 June 2026 and numbered 2026/1183, the summary of which was published on 10 August 2026, the Board imposed an administrative fine of TRY 1,000,000 for breach of the data security obligations under Article 12 of the KVKK on a savings finance company that had used contact information collected through a brand ambassador program for marketing via SMS messages and phone calls without relying on any condition for processing personal data. You may access the Authority’s announcement in Turkish here , our announcement on this topic here , the decision summary in Turkish here , and our announcement on the decision summary here . items.headline: Foreign Policy on what the Dublin summit actually decided

items.body: Welcome back to World Brief, where we’re looking at the European Union ’s artificial intelligence ambitions, dual car bombings in Russia , and an alleged Iranian strike on a U.S. radar system. European Union leaders convened in Dublin on Friday for the bloc’s first-ever summit on artificial intelligence. With the continent expected to fall short of its chip-manufacturing goals, the conference may be a pivotal opportunity for the EU to develop a unified policy that aims to catch up with the world’s AI powerhouses : the United States and China. Welcome back to World Brief, where we’re looking at the European Union ’s artificial intelligence ambitions, dual car bombings in Russia , and an alleged Iranian strike on a U.S. radar system. European Union leaders convened in Dublin on Friday for the bloc’s first-ever summit on artificial intelligence. With the continent expected to fall short of its chip-manufacturing goals, the conference may be a pivotal opportunity for the EU to develop a unified policy that aims to catch up with the world’s AI powerhouses : the United States and China. The 2023 European Chips Act sought to double the continent’s semiconductor production global market share from roughly 10 percent to 20 percent by 2030 and attract billions of dollars in foreign tech investment. This legislation was a way for Europeans to say, “we want to be serious about this, and the only way to be competitive is to engage in the same practices, because otherwise you’re just never going to get manufacturing back to your shores,” Bruce Andrews, then-Intel’s corporate vice president, told FP’s Rishi Iyengar in 2024. Since then, though, the EU has emerged as a more passive actor in AI’s advancement. A March report by Eurostat , the bloc’s statistics office, found that 1 in 5 EU enterprises used at least one AI technology in 2025, compared to less than 1 in 10 businesses a few years ago. Yet, in installed data center capacity alone, the bloc, with its 11.92 gigawatts, remains double-digits behind the United States (53.73 gigawatts) and China (31.9 gigawatts). Yet the summit’s AI agenda may be derailed by other issues —particularly, who will represent European interests in future Russia-Ukraine peace talks. On Thursday, Russian President Vladimir Putin told U.S. special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner that he would allow European officials to join the next round of negotiations.
